The bridge E-F, which every path from the triangles to the tail must cross, is thickest and in accent at 0.48, ahead of C-E at 0.36 and F-G at 0.29; the triangle edges A-B and C-D carry the least, 0.07." width="100%"} Edge betweenness centrality measures how many shortest paths run through each edge. For every pair of nodes, each shortest path between them contributes to the edges it uses; when a pair has several shortest paths, each one counts for an equal share. Edges with high scores carry a lot of the graph's traffic: they are bridges between clusters, bottlenecks, and the first links to fail or congest. This is the edge counterpart of `betweenness_centrality()`, and it is the quantity that the Girvan-Newman method (`cmty_edge_btwns()`, `cmty_girvan_newman()`) removes edges by to split a graph into communities. Use it on its own to: - find the links whose loss would most lengthen paths in a network - spot inter-community edges before running community detection - weight or prune edges by how structurally important they are Parallel edges are separate routes and split their shared paths between them; self-loops score `0`. On a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) shortest paths minimize total edge weight (Dijkstra's algorithm), so only the cheapest parallel edges carry paths; on an unweighted graph they minimize hops. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), divide scores by `n * (n - 1)`, the number of ordered node pairs, so they fall in `[0, 1]`. If `False`, return raw path counts (halved for undirected graphs so that each unordered pair is counted once). Both match NetworkX's `edge_betweenness_centrality()`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure distances by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph: weights are used on a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) and hop counts otherwise, the same rule `shortest_path()` uses. Pass `True` or `False` to override. Edges without a weight count as `1.0`; weights must be non-negative. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the edge attribute to store the scores in. If `None` (default), automatically uses `"edge_betweenness_centrality"`. Overwrites the attribute if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as an edge attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping edge IDs to betweenness scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~betweenness_centrality`) : The same count for nodes. [](`~edge_load_centrality`) : A close relative that splits paths evenly at each step. [](`~cmty_girvan_newman`) : Find communities by removing the busiest edges. [](`~edge_betweenness_centrality_subset`) : Count only paths between chosen sources and targets. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by a single edge: every path from one triangle to the other must cross the bridge, so it has by far the highest score: ::: {#469dc46e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")] ) ( graph.edge_betweenness_centrality() .get_edge_df(labels=True) .select("source", "target", "edge_betweenness_centrality") .sort("edge_betweenness_centrality", descending=True) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

Drawn with each edge as wide and as dark as its score, and the members colored by faction, the heaviest edges either cross the split or lead from the instructor to members 4, 5, 6, 10 and 16, who reach the rest of the club only through the instructor: ::: {#b00836d2 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} club.plot( layout="pos", color_by="faction", label_by="label", edge_width=2, edge_width_by="edge_betweenness_centrality", edge_color_by="edge_betweenness_centrality", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: That's what the Girvan-Newman method, `cmty_girvan_newman()`, builds on: it removes the edge with the highest score, recomputes, and repeats until the graph falls apart. ### Bridges and bottlenecks The metro is weighted by travel time, so the scores count the fastest routes: ::: {#9410f6f4 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} metro = ec.metro().edge_betweenness_centrality() ( metro.get_edge_df(labels=True) .select("source", "target", "line", "edge_betweenness_centrality") .sort("edge_betweenness_centrality", descending=True) .head(4) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

Eastfield can also be reached through Lakeside, but going through Market is quicker, so the trips to the east and the Airport take it: ::: {#df3f83dd .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} metro.plot( layout="pos", label_by="label", edge_width=2, edge_width_by="edge_betweenness_centrality", edge_color_by="edge_betweenness_centrality", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: For routes between chosen sources and targets only, use `edge_betweenness_centrality_subset()`; to count flow along every path rather than the shortest ones, `edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality()`.
